metadata.methods_description: EEG data were recorded using a Brain Products actiCHamp Plus system with BrainVision Recorder (v1.25.0101) and a 32-channel actiCAP slim active electrode system mounted per the international 10/20 system. The ground electrode was placed at FPz, two electrodes were repurposed for mastoid referencing, and three electrodes recorded EOG (horizontal and vertical). Data were sampled at 500 Hz and referenced to Cz. StimTrak was used to assess stimulus presentation delays (~20 ms) for visual and auditory stimuli.

citation_details.title: Benchmarking ERP Analysis: Manual Features, Deep Learning, and Foundation Models
citation_details.author: Yihe Wang, Zhiqi Kang, Bo Chen, Yu Zhang, Xiang Zhang
citation_details.abstract: Event-related potential (ERP), a specialized paradigm of electroencephalographic (EEG), reflects neurological responses to external stimuli or events, generally associated with the brain's processing of specific cognitive tasks. ERP plays a critical role in cognitive analysis, the detection of neurological diseases, and the assessment of psychological states. Recent years have seen substantial advances in deep learning-based methods for spontaneous EEG and other non-time-locked task-related EEG signals. However, their effectiveness on ERP data remains underexplored, and many existing ERP studies still rely heavily on manually extracted features. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive benchmark study that systematically compares traditional manual features (followed by a linear classifier), deep learning models, and pre-trained EEG foundation models for ERP analysis. citation_details.title: Laya: A LeJEPA Approach to EEG via Latent Prediction over Reconstruction
citation_details.author: S. Panchavati, Uddhav Panchavati, Hiroki Nariai, Corey W. Arnold, W. Speier
citation_details.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used tool for studying brain function, with applications in clinical neuroscience, diagnosis, and brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). Recent EEG foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora aim to learn transferable representations, but their effectiveness remains unclear; reported improvements over smaller task-specific models are often modest, sensitive to downstream adaptation and fine-tuning strategies, and limited under linear probing. citation_details.title: Integrating socioeconomic context with multimodal EEG data for improved ADHD risk screening
citation_details.author: Sadikul Haque Sadi, Md. Arman Hossain, Md. Nurul Ahad Tawhid
citation_details.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects millions globally, yet current diagnostic approaches rely on subjective behavioral assessments without objective neurophysiological markers. While machine learning on electroencephalogram (EEG) data shows promise for automated ADHD risk screening, current methods focus only on brain signals and ignore socioeconomic factors that strongly affect neurodevelopment and ADHD risk. citation_details.title: Early-life family socioeconomic and educational impacts on adult EEG and behavioral signatures of visual cognitive function
citation_details.author: Shuxuan Mao, Xuan Zhang, Fengrui Zhang
citation_details.abstract: Socioeconomic and educational background is associated with individual differences in cognitive performance, yet how different socioeconomic indicators relate to adult brain function remains unclear. Using an open-access dataset, we analyzed electroencephalography (EEG) and behavioral data from 73 young adults performing the flanker and visual search tasks. Event-related potentials (P1, P2, N2, and P3) and alpha-beta band time-frequency features were extracted to characterize sensory processing, cognitive control, and attentional engagement. Four socioeconomic indicators were examined: subjective family socioeconomic status (SES), household income, parental education, and participants' own educational attainment. citation_details.title: A Minimal EEG Montage for Adult ADHD Detection: Discovering the Frontoparietal Beta–Theta Framework Via Explainable AI
citation_details.author: Sadikul Haque Sadi, Md. Nurul Ahad Tawhid
citation_details.abstract: Current deep learning models for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnostics rely on opaque, high-density electroencephalography (EEG) arrays, limiting their clinical utility. This study aims to transition adult ADHD screening from an uninterpretable “closed box” into a transparent, scalable framework by identifying the minimal neurobiological features required for accurate detection. We have developed a multimodal deep learning architecture to classify adult ADHD-screened-positive individuals versus neurotypical controls using EEG data recorded during demanding executive functioning tasks. citation_details.title: Adaptive Split-MMD Training for Small-Sample Cross-Dataset P300 EEG Classification
citation_details.author: Weiyu Chen, A. Delorme
citation_details.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
citation_details.abstract: Detecting single-trial P300 from EEG is difficult when only a few labeled trials are available. When attempting to boost a small target set with a large source dataset through transfer learning, cross-dataset shift arises. To address this challenge, we study transfer between two public visual-oddball ERP datasets using five shared electrodes (Fz, Pz, P3, P4, Oz) under a strict small-sample regime (target: 10 trials/subject; source: 80 trials/subject). We introduce Adaptive Split Maximum Mean Discrepancy Training (AS-MMD), which combines (i) a target-weighted loss with warm-up tied to the square root of the source/target size ratio, (ii) Split Batch Normalization (Split-BN) with shared affine parameters and per-domain running statistics, and (iii) a parameter-free logit-level Radial Basis Function kernel Maximum Mean Discrepancy (RBF-MMD) term using the median-bandwidth heuristic. Implemented on an EEG Conformer, AS-MMD is backbone-agnostic and leaves the inference-time model unchanged.
